This weight depends only on the Y-coordinate: neighbors above ($yn>0$) contribute 2, neighbors below ($yn<0$) contribute 0, and neighbors at the same level ($yn=0$) contribute 1 [S3, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S3] explicitly describes the calculation of the occlusion dimension 'dim'. It states: 'For each neighbor, if it is not empty, add (1 + yk1 - yk2) to dim, where yk1=1 if yn>0 else 0, and yk2=1 if yn<0 else 0.' Analyzing this formula for non-empty neighbors: 1. If yn > 0, yk1=1 and yk2=0, so the contribution is 1 + 1 - 0 = 2. 2. If yn < 0, yk1=0 and yk2=1, so the contribution is 1 + 0 - 1 = 0. 3. If yn = 0, yk1=0 and yk2=0, so the contribution is 1 + 0 - 0 = 1. This matches the claim exactly.
